package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via Smoke Loader, not a public package repository)
package_info.why_malicious: Whiffy Recon is considered malicious because it is a geo-location malware that continuously scans for nearby Wi-Fi networks and exfiltrates the victim's physical location using the Google Geolocation API, enabling persistent surveillance and privacy invasion.

execution_context.file_location: main malware payload (delivered post-infection by Smoke Loader)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code continuously scans for nearby Wi-Fi networks, sends the list to the Google Geolocation API to determine the device's physical location, and exfiltrates this location data to a command-and-control server, enabling real-time tracking of the victim.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Continuous Wi-Fi scanning and exfiltration of geolocation data is highly unusual for legitimate software and is a hallmark of surveillance malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not repeatedly scan for Wi-Fi networks and send geolocation data to external servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate location-based services (e.g., mapping apps) may use Wi-Fi scanning and geolocation APIs, but only with explicit user permission and not for continuous, covert tracking.
key_indicators: Automated use of Google Geolocation API
Exfiltration of location data to C2 infrastructure
Operation without user interaction or consent

attack_chain.action: Initial infection via Smoke Loader, which downloads and executes Whiffy Recon payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of Whiffy Recon malware on victim system

attack_chain.action: Whiffy Recon executes and begins continuous scanning of nearby Wi-Fi networks.
Wi-Fi network data is sent to Google Geolocation API to determine physical location.
Victim's geolocation data is exfiltrated to the attacker's command-and-control server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent tracking and surveillance of victim

behavioral_signatures: Continuous or periodic Wi-Fi network scanning by non-network management processes
Automated queries to Google Geolocation API from unexpected applications
Regular exfiltration of geolocation data to external servers
file_indicators: Presence of unknown executables delivered by Smoke Loader
Malware persistence mechanisms (e.g., registry run keys, scheduled tasks) associated with Whiffy Recon
network_indicators: Frequent outbound connections to Google Geolocation API endpoints
Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure associated with Whiffy Recon or Smoke Loader
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes that repeatedly scan for Wi-Fi networks and make automated requests to the Google Geolocation API. Correlate with outbound traffic to suspicious C2 domains. Flag unknown binaries delivered by Smoke Loader, and alert on persistence mechanisms linked to these payloads. Use behavioral analytics to detect continuous geolocation exfiltration activity.
